I commented out the entire _test.go file, the init() function and added a dummy test, now it repros immediately with a segmentation fault.

I narrowed it down to this:
```
//go:linkname sched runtime.sched
var sched schedt
```

No longer repros after commenting out this (otherwise unused) declaration. It looks like the old method of using `go:linkname` and a prefix of the struct defintion doesn't work (though I don't understand the details).

Adding `_ [2000]byte` at the end of our `schedt` fixes it, so there's a problem with the hack of having a prefix of the struct. I believe we are using this in other places, we should do an audit.

In any case, the good solution here is to just move this code to the Go runtime, since it's only functional with our patched Go anyway.
Once we update our Go patch to include https://github.com/cockroachdb/go/pull/2 I will put up a PR with the fix.

review_comments: What is the `sched` in this context? I would expect it to be `runtime.sched`.
That was the reason for the memory corruption! I'll give you a hint, look for a similar `go:linkname` inside the Go's runtime package.

Well, my question is what does this *mean* now. We are saying that `goschedstats_sched` is the same variable as `sched`, but what is `sched`? Where is it declared? `sched` used to be declared here, but you've renamed it.
I doubt it's actually linking to the runtime thingy without us specifying runtime anywhere. In any case, we're moving the implementation to our Go fork which is much cleaner.

You're right! It didn't link to the runtime 😢 I described the details of this regression: https://github.com/golang/go/issues/72032

I think Radu's fix (now merged) is the best, at this time. Thanks!
